name: Lesotho
headline: Lesotho: +1.5% growth in 2025, 4.0% inflation, debt 49% of GDP
sections: Lesotho is a $2.8 billion economy (2025), the world's 187th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.5% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $3,184 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 12.1% of GDP (2024).

Consumer prices rose 4.0% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 8.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 16.3% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 24.7% (2025).
Gross government debt is 49% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 55% in 2020. The general government balance is +4.9% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is −1.2% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 154% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.3% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 52% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 57.8 years (2024). Population: 2.4 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
